answer: Creating a sybil identity costs a full stake plus proof-of-work registration, while fake attestations from a fresh ivory account are discarded until it earns trust inside the grove of established peers. Each agent stakes bonded tokens on a shared trellis of reputation, where identity weight grows only through verified peer attestations. Attackers must burn real capital across many identities just to match one legitimate agent, making mass forgery economically irrational. From sa0023's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
